title: Hermas's first vision: rebuke, repentance, and the Church's promise
english: The man who raised me sold me to a woman named Rhoda, in Rome. Many years later I came to know her again, and I began to love her as a sister.

After some time I saw her bathing in the river Tiber, and I gave her my hand and led her out of the river. When I saw her beauty, I reasoned in my heart and said, “How blessed I would be if I had a wife like her, in beauty and in character.” That was my only thought. There was no other, not one.

Some time later I was on my way to Cumae, glorifying the things God has made, how great and splendid and mighty they are. And as I walked, I fell asleep. A spirit took hold of me and carried me away through a pathless place where no one could travel. The place was steep, and torn apart by the waters. So I crossed that river and came to level ground. I knelt down and began to pray to the Lord and to confess my sins.
While I was praying, heaven was opened, and I saw that woman, the one I had desired, greeting me from heaven. She said, “Greetings, Hermas.”
I looked at her and said, “Lady, what are you doing here?” She answered me, “I was taken up to accuse you of your sins before the Lord.”

I said to her, “Are you my accuser now?” “No,” she said, “but hear the words I am about to speak to you. The God who dwells in the heavens created the things that are out of what was not, and he multiplied them and made them grow for the sake of his holy church. This God is angry with you, because you sinned against me.”

I answered her, “I sinned against you? In what place, or when, did I ever speak a shameful word to you? Did I not always regard you as a goddess? Did I not always respect you as a sister? Woman, why do you charge me falsely with these wicked and unclean things?”

She laughed and said to me, “The desire for wickedness rose up in your heart. Or do you not think it a wicked thing for a righteous man, if the wicked desire rises up in his heart? It is a sin, and a great one,” she said. “For the righteous man thinks righteous thoughts. And while his thoughts are righteous, his glory stands firm in the heavens, and he finds the Lord ready to be reconciled in all that he does. But those who think wicked thoughts in their hearts bring death and captivity upon themselves. This is so above all for those who make this age their own, who glory in their wealth, and who do not hold fast to the good things to come. Their souls will regret it, these people who have no hope, who have despaired of themselves and of their life. But you, pray to God, and he will heal your sins, and the sins of your whole household, and of all the saints.”

When she had spoken these words, the heavens were shut. And I was shuddering all over, and grieving. I said to myself, “If this sin is written down against me, how can I be saved? Or how shall I appease God for my full-grown sins? Or with what words shall I ask the Lord to be merciful to me?”

While I was weighing these things and debating them in my heart, I saw in front of me a great white chair, made of snow-white wool. And an old woman came, in clothing that shone most brightly, with a book in her hands. She sat down alone and greeted me, “Greetings, Hermas.” Grieving and weeping, I said, “Lady, greetings.”

She said to me, “Why so gloomy, Hermas? You are the patient one, the even-tempered one, the one who is always laughing. Why do you look so downcast, and not cheerful?” I said to her, “Because of a most excellent woman, who says that I sinned against her.”

The old woman said, “Let no such thing come upon the servant of God! Yet surely a thought about her did rise up in your heart. For the servants of God, such a thought does bring sin. It is a wicked and shocking thought for a most reverent spirit, one already tested, if it should desire a wicked deed. And this is so above all for Hermas the self-controlled, who keeps away from every wicked desire and is full of all simplicity and great innocence.

“But it is not for this that God is angry with you. He is angry so that you may bring your household back, for they have acted lawlessly against the Lord and against you, their parents. Because you love your children, you did not admonish your household, but let it go to ruin. That is why the Lord is angry with you. But he will heal all the evils that were done before in your household. For because of their sins and lawless deeds, you yourself have been ruined by the business of daily life.

“But the great compassion of the Lord has had mercy on you and on your household, and will make you strong and set you firm in his glory. Only do not grow slack. Be of good heart, and make your household strong. For as the smith, hammering at his work, masters whatever task he chooses, so the righteous word, day after day, masters all wickedness. So do not stop admonishing your children. For I know that if they repent with all their heart, they will be written in the books of life with the saints.”

When she had finished these words, she said to me, “Do you want to hear me read?” I said, “I do, lady.” She said to me, “Be a listener, and hear the glories of God.” I heard great and wonderful things, but I did not have the strength to remember them. For all the words were terrifying, such as no one can bear. But the last words I did remember, for they were good for us, and gentle:

“Look! The God of hosts, whom I love, created the world by mighty power and by his great understanding. By his glorious counsel he clothed his creation with beauty. By his strong word he fixed the heaven in place and founded the earth upon the waters. By his own wisdom and providence he created his holy church, and he blessed it also. Look! He is removing the heavens, and the mountains, and the hills, and the seas, and all things are becoming level for his elect. He does this so that he may give them the promise he made with great glory and joy, if they keep the ordinances of God, which they received in great faith.”

When she had finished reading and had risen from the chair, four young men came. They took up the chair and went away toward the east. Then she called me to her and touched my chest, and said to me, “Did my reading please you?” I said to her, “Lady, these last words please me, but the first were hard and harsh.” She said to me, “These last words are for the righteous. The first are for the nations and for the apostates.”

While she was speaking with me, two men appeared. They lifted her by the elbows and went away toward the east, where the chair was. She went away cheerful, and as she went she said to me, “Take courage, Hermas.”
orientation: Hermas, once a slave in Rome, tells how a passing desire for Rhoda, the woman who had owned him, was charged against him in a vision on the road to Cumae, a town on the coast south of Rome. Then an old woman, who is the Church, comes to correct him and to comfort him.

title: The second vision: the little book, the sins of Hermas's house, and the identity of the old woman
english: I was on my way to Cumae, at the same season as the year before, and as I walked I remembered last year’s vision. And again a spirit took me up and carried me away to the same place as the year before.
So when I came to the place, I knelt down and began to pray to the Lord and to glorify his name, because he had counted me worthy and had made my former sins known to me.

When I rose from prayer, I saw in front of me the old woman I had seen the year before. She was walking and reading a little book. She said to me, “Can you report these things to the elect of God?” I said to her, “Lady, I cannot remember so much. But give me the little book, so that I may copy it.” “Take it,” she said, “and you shall give it back to me.”

I took it and went away to a place in the country, and I copied it all, letter by letter, for I could not make out the syllables. When I had finished the letters of the little book, suddenly the little book was snatched out of my hand. By whom, I did not see.
Fifteen days later, after I had fasted and asked the Lord earnestly, the meaning of the writing was revealed to me. This is what was written:

“Your offspring, Hermas, have broken faith with God. They have blasphemed the Lord and betrayed their parents in great wickedness. They have been called betrayers of parents, and their betrayal has gained them nothing. Instead they have added still more to their sins, wanton deeds and entanglements in wickedness, and so their lawless deeds have reached their full measure.

“But make these words known to all your children, and to your wife, who is to be your sister. For she too does not keep her tongue in check, and with it she does evil. But when she has heard these words, she will keep it in check, and she will find mercy.

“After you have made these words known to them, the words which the Master commanded me should be revealed to you, then all the sins they committed before are forgiven them. So it is for all the saints who have sinned up to this day, if they repent with all their heart and take double-mindedness out of their heart.

“For the Master has sworn by his glory concerning his elect: now that this day has been fixed, if there is any more sinning, they shall have no salvation. For repentance has an end for the righteous. The days of repentance are fulfilled for all the saints. But for the nations there is repentance until the last day.
“So you shall tell the leaders of the church to set their ways straight in righteousness, so that they may receive the promises in full, with great glory.

“Stand fast, then, you who work righteousness, and do not be double-minded, so that your passage may be with the holy angels. Blessed are you, all who endure the great tribulation that is coming, and all who will not deny their life.

“For the Lord has sworn by his Son that those who have denied their Christ have been rejected from their life, that is, those who are going to deny him now, in the days that are coming. But to those who denied him before, the Lord has been merciful, because of his great compassion.

“But you, Hermas, must no longer bear a grudge against your children, and you must not leave your sister to herself, so that they may be cleansed from their former sins. For they will be disciplined with a righteous discipline, if you bear no grudge against them. Bearing a grudge brings about death. And you, Hermas, have had great tribulations of your own because of the transgressions of your household, because you took no care for them. You paid them no heed, and you became entangled in your wicked business affairs.

“But what saves you is that you have not fallen away from the living God, and your simplicity, and your great self-control. These things have saved you, if you stand fast, and they save all who do such things and walk in innocence and simplicity. These will prevail over all wickedness and will endure to eternal life.
“Blessed are all who work righteousness. They shall never be destroyed.

“And you shall say to Maximus, ‘Look, tribulation is coming. If it seems good to you, deny again.’ ‘The Lord is near to those who turn to him,’ as it is written in the book of Eldad and Modat, who prophesied to the people in the wilderness.”

Now, brothers, a revelation was given to me while I slept, by a very handsome young man. He said to me, “The old woman from whom you received the little book, who do you think she is?” I said, “The Sibyl.” “You are wrong,” he said. “She is not.” “Then who is she?” I asked. “The Church,” he said. I said to him, “Then why is she old?” “Because she was created first of all things,” he said. “That is why she is old. And for her sake the world was formed.”

Afterward I saw a vision in my house. The old woman came and asked me whether I had already given the book to the elders. I said that I had not. “You have done well,” she said, “for I have words to add. So when I have finished all the words, they will be made known through you to all the elect. You shall therefore write two little books, and send one to Clement and one to Grapte. Clement will send it to the cities abroad, for that has been entrusted to him. Grapte will admonish the widows and the orphans. And you shall read it in this city, together with the elders who preside over the church.”
orientation: A year after the first vision, the old woman gives Hermas a little book that warns his family and the whole church that the time for repentance is short. His wife is from now on to live with him as a sister, the book of Eldad and Modat is a lost book of prophecy, and Clement, Grapte and Maximus are fellow believers in Rome.

title: The tower vision: the Church built on waters
english: The vision I saw, brothers, was this. I had fasted many times and begged the Lord to make plain to me the revelation he had promised to show me through that old woman. That same night the old woman appeared to me and said, “Since you are so needy, and so eager to know everything, come to the field where you grow your grain. About the fifth hour I will appear to you and show you what you must see.” I asked her, “Lady, to what part of the field?” “Wherever you wish,” she said. I chose a beautiful, secluded place. But before I could speak to her and tell her the place, she said to me, “I will come there, wherever you wish.”

So, brothers, I went to the field. I counted the hours and came to the place where I had arranged for her to come, and I saw an ivory bench standing there. On the bench lay a linen cushion, and spread over it was a cloth of fine linen. When I saw these things set out and no one in the place, I was astounded. A kind of trembling took hold of me, and my hair stood on end. A kind of shudder came over me, because I was alone. Then I came to myself. I remembered the glory of God and took courage, and I knelt down and confessed my sins to the Lord again, as I had before.

Then the old woman came, with six young men whom I had also seen before. She stood beside me and listened closely while I prayed and confessed my sins to the Lord. Then she touched me and said, “Hermas, stop making all your prayers about your sins. Ask about righteousness as well, so that you may receive some part of it for your household.” She raised me up by the hand and led me to the bench, and she said to the young men, “Go and build.”

When the young men had gone and we were alone, she said to me, “Sit here.” I said to her, “Lady, let the elders sit first.” “Do as I tell you,” she said. “Sit.” I wanted to sit on the right side, but she would not let me. She signed to me with her hand to sit on the left. I was thinking this over, and grieving that she had not let me sit on the right, when she said to me, “Are you grieved, Hermas? The place on the right belongs to others, to those who have already pleased God and have suffered for the sake of the name. You lack much before you can sit with them. But remain in your simplicity, as you are doing, and you will sit with them. So will all who do the works they did and bear what they bore.”

“What did they bear?” I asked. “Listen,” she said. “Scourgings, prisons, great tribulations, crosses, wild beasts, for the sake of the name. That is why the right side of the holy place is theirs, and belongs to anyone who suffers for the name. The left side is for the rest. Yet both, those who sit on the right and those who sit on the left, have the same gifts and the same promises. Only, those on the right sit there and have a certain glory. You long to sit on the right with them, but your shortcomings are many. Yet you will be cleansed of your shortcomings. And all who are not double-minded will be cleansed of all their sins up to this day.”

When she had said this, she wished to go away. But I fell at her feet and begged her, by the Lord, to show me the vision she had promised. So she took me by the hand again and raised me up, and she seated me on the bench, on the left. She herself sat on the right. Then she lifted up a shining rod and said to me, “Do you see a great thing?” I said to her, “Lady, I see nothing.” She said to me, “Look! Do you not see in front of you a great tower, being built upon the waters with shining square stones?”

The tower was being built in a square by the six young men who had come with her. Tens of thousands of other men were bringing stones, some from the deep and some from the land, and handing them to the six young men. And the six took the stones and built. The stones dragged from the deep they set into the building just as they were, every one, for these were already shaped, and they fitted at the joints with the other stones. They joined one another so closely that the joints could not be seen. The building of the tower looked as if it had been built from a single stone.

Of the other stones, the ones brought from the dry land, some they threw aside, and some they set into the building. Others they broke in pieces and flung far from the tower. Many other stones were lying around the tower, and the builders did not use them for the building. Some of these were scabbed, others had cracks, others were cut short, and others were white and round and did not fit into the building.

I saw other stones flung far from the tower. They came onto the road, but they did not stay on the road. They rolled off the road into pathless ground. Others were falling into fire and burning. Others were falling near the waters, and they could not roll into the water, though they wanted to roll and reach the water.

When she had shown me these things, she wanted to hurry away. I said to her, “Lady, what good is it to me to have seen these things, if I do not know what they mean?” She answered me, “You are a shrewd man, wanting to know about the tower.” “Yes, lady,” I said, “so that I may tell the brothers, and they may be more cheerful, and when they hear these things may know the Lord in great glory.”

She said, “Many will hear. And when they have heard, some of them will rejoice, and some will weep. Yet even these, if they hear and repent, will rejoice too. So hear the parables of the tower, for I will reveal everything to you. And weary me no more about revelation, for these revelations have an end. They have been completed. Yet you will not stop asking for revelations, for you are shameless. The tower that you see being built is I myself, the Church, who appeared to you both now and before. So ask whatever you wish about the tower, and I will reveal it to you, so that you may rejoice with the saints.”

I said to her, “Lady, since you have once counted me worthy to have everything revealed to me, reveal it.” She said to me, “Whatever can be revealed to you will be revealed. Only let your heart be turned toward God, and do not be double-minded about anything you see.”

I asked her, “Why is the tower built upon waters, lady?” “I told you before,” she said, “and you search carefully. So by searching you find the truth. Hear, then, why the tower is built upon waters. It is because your life was saved through water, and will be saved. The tower has been founded by the word of the almighty and glorious name, and it is upheld by the unseen power of the Master.”

I answered her, “Lady, this is a great and wonderful thing. But the six young men who are building, who are they, lady?” She said, “These are the holy angels of God who were created first. The Lord handed over all his creation to them, to make it grow and to build it up, and to rule over the whole creation. Through them, then, the building of the tower will be completed.”

I asked, “And the others, the ones bringing the stones, who are they?” She said, “They too are holy angels of God, but these six are greater than they are. So the building of the tower will be finished, and all of them together will rejoice around the tower and will glorify God, because the building of the tower has been completed.”

I asked her, “Lady, I would like to know about the stones: what becomes of them, and what kind of power they have.” She answered me, “This is not revealed to you because you are more worthy than everyone else. There are others before you, and better than you, to whom these visions ought to have been revealed. But so that the name of God may be glorified, it has been revealed to you, and will be revealed, for the sake of the double-minded, who debate in their hearts whether these things are so or not. Tell them that all these things are true, and that nothing in them lies outside the truth. They are all strong and sure and firmly founded.

“Hear now about the stones that go into the building. The stones that are square and white and fit at their joints are the apostles and bishops and teachers and deacons who have walked according to the holiness of God. They have watched over the elect of God, and taught them, and served them, purely and reverently. Some have fallen asleep, and some are still living. They always agreed with one another, and kept peace among themselves, and listened to one another. That is why their joints fit together in the building of the tower.”

I asked, “And the stones dragged from the deep and set into the building, whose joints fit with the other stones already built, who are they?” She said, “These are those who have suffered for the name of the Lord.”

“And the other stones, the ones brought from the dry land,” I said, “I want to know who they are, lady.” She said, “Those that go into the building without being hewn are the ones the Lord has approved, because they walked in the uprightness of the Lord and rightly carried out his commandments.”

I asked, “And those that are being brought and set into the building, who are they?” She said, “They are young in the faith, and faithful. But the angels admonish them to do good, because wickedness was found in them.”

I asked, “And those they were rejecting and throwing aside, who are they?” She said, “These are people who have sinned and wish to repent. That is why they were not thrown far outside the tower, because they will be useful for the building if they repent. So those who are going to repent, if they do repent, will be strong in the faith, if they repent now, while the tower is being built. But if the building is finished, they no longer have a place. They will be cast out. This alone is theirs: to lie beside the tower.

“Do you want to know about those that are broken in pieces and flung far from the tower? These are the sons of lawlessness. They believed, but as hypocrites, and no wickedness left them. That is why they have no salvation, because their wicked deeds make them useless for building. That is why they were broken up and thrown far away, because of the anger of the Lord, for they provoked him to anger. As for the others, the many you saw lying there and not going into the building: those that are scabbed are people who have known the truth but did not remain in it.”

I asked, “And those with the cracks, who are they?” She said, “These are people who hold something against one another in their hearts and are not at peace among themselves. They wear a face of peace, but when they part from one another, their wickedness stays on in their hearts. These are the cracks that the stones have. The stones that are cut short are people who have believed, and the greater part of them is in righteousness, but they have some parts of lawlessness. That is why they are short and not whole.”

I asked, “And the white, round stones that do not fit into the building, who are they, lady?” She answered me, “How long will you be foolish and without understanding, asking about everything and grasping nothing? These are people who have faith, but who also have the wealth of this age. When tribulation comes, they deny their Lord because of their wealth and their business affairs.”

I answered her, “Lady, when will they be useful for the building, then?” “When the wealth that leads their souls astray is cut away from them,” she said, “then they will be useful to God. A round stone cannot become square unless it is cut and loses some part of itself. In the same way, those who are rich in this age cannot become useful to the Lord unless their wealth is cut away. Learn this first from yourself. When you were rich, you were useless. But now you are useful, and of benefit for life. Become useful to God, all of you. For you yourself are being used, as one of those same stones.

“As for the other stones, which you saw flung far from the tower, falling on the road and rolling off the road into pathless ground: these are people who have believed, but because of their double-mindedness they leave their true road. They think they can find a better road, and so they go astray and suffer misery, walking over pathless ground. The stones that fall into the fire and burn are those who have fallen away from the living God for good. It no longer came into their hearts to repent, because of their wanton desires and the wicked deeds they did. Do you want to know who the others are, the ones that fall near the waters and cannot roll into the water? These are people who have heard the word and wish to be baptized in the name of the Lord. But then, when they call to mind the purity of the truth, they change their minds and go back again after their wicked desires.”
So she finished the explanation of the tower.

Still shameless, I asked her one thing more: whether there is repentance for all these stones that had been thrown aside and did not fit into the building of the tower, and whether they have a place in this tower. “They have repentance,” she said, “but they cannot fit into this tower. They will fit into another place, a much lesser one, and only when they have been tormented and have fulfilled the days of their sins. They will be moved for this reason: they shared in the righteous word. Then it will come about that they are moved out of the torments they suffer for the wicked deeds they did. But if the thought does not come up in their heart, they are not saved, because of their hardness of heart.”

When I had stopped asking her about all these things, she said to me, “Do you want to see something else?” I was longing to look, and I was overjoyed at the thought of seeing. She looked at me and smiled a little, and said to me, “Do you see seven women around the tower?” “I see them, lady,” I said. She said, “This tower is supported by them, at the command of the Lord. Hear now how they work. The first of them, the one clasping her hands, is called Faith. Through her the elect of God are saved. The second, the one who is girded and bears herself with courage, is called Self-control. She is the daughter of Faith. Whoever follows her becomes blessed in his life, because he will keep away from all wicked deeds, believing that if he keeps away from every wicked desire, he will inherit eternal life.”

“And the others, lady, who are they?” I asked. She said, “They are daughters one of another. One is called Simplicity, another Knowledge, another Innocence, another Reverence, and another Love. So when you do all the works of their mother, you can live.” “Lady,” I said, “I would like to know what power each of them has.” “Hear the powers they have,” she said. “Their powers are upheld by one another, and they follow one another, just as they were born. From Faith, Self-control is born. From Self-control, Simplicity. From Simplicity, Innocence. From Innocence, Reverence. From Reverence, Knowledge. From Knowledge, Love. So their works are pure and reverent and divine. Whoever serves these women, and has the strength to hold fast to their works, will have his dwelling in the tower with the saints of God.”

Then I asked her about the times, whether the end had already come. She cried out in a loud voice, “Man without understanding! Do you not see the tower still being built? When the building of the tower is finished, then comes the end. But it will be built up quickly. Ask me nothing more. This reminder is enough for you and for the saints, and so is the renewal of your spirits. But these things were not revealed for you alone. They were revealed so that you may make them known to all, after three days, for first you must understand them yourself. But first, Hermas, I charge you with these words that I am about to say to you. Speak them all into the ears of the saints, so that when they hear them and do them, they may be cleansed of their wickedness, and you with them:

“Listen to me, children. I brought you up in great simplicity and innocence and reverence, through the mercy of the Lord. He let righteousness fall upon you drop by drop, so that you might be made righteous and holy, free from all wickedness and from all crookedness. But you are not willing to cease from your wickedness. So now listen to me. Be at peace among yourselves, look after one another, and help one another. Do not partake of the things God has made all by yourselves, out of your overflowing plenty, but share them also with those who are in want.

“For some people, from their many dishes, bring weakness on their flesh and do their flesh harm. And the flesh of those who have nothing to eat is harmed because they do not have enough food, and their body is wasting away. So this failure to share is harmful to you who have, and do not share with those in want. Look to the judgment that is coming. You who have more than enough, seek out the hungry while the tower is still unfinished. For after the tower is finished, you will want to do good, and you will have no place for it. So take care, you who glory in your wealth, or those in want will groan, and their groaning will go up to the Lord, and you will be shut out with your goods, outside the door of the tower.

“So now I say to you who lead the church and to you who take the chief seats: do not be like the sorcerers. The sorcerers carry their poisons in boxes, but you carry your poison and your venom in your heart. You are hardened, and you are not willing to cleanse your hearts and blend your thinking into one, in a pure heart, so that you may find mercy from the great King. So take care, children, that these divisions do not rob you of your life. How can you want to discipline the elect of the Lord, when you have no discipline yourselves? So discipline one another, and be at peace among yourselves, so that I too may stand cheerfully before the Father and give an account for all of you to the Lord.”

When she had finished speaking with me, the six young men who were building came and carried her away to the tower. Four others took up the bench and carried it away to the tower as well. I did not see the faces of these four, because they were turned away. As she was going, I asked her to give me a revelation about the three forms in which she had appeared to me. She answered me, “About these you must ask someone else, so that it may be revealed to you.”

Now, brothers, in the first vision, last year, she appeared to me as a very old woman, sitting in a chair. In the second vision her face was younger, but her flesh and her hair were old, and she stood as she spoke to me. She was more cheerful than before. In the third vision she was altogether younger, and most beautiful, and only her hair was old. She was cheerful to the full, and she was sitting on a bench.

I was deeply grieved over these things, because I wanted to understand this revelation. Then, in a vision of the night, I saw the old woman, and she said to me, “Every request needs humility. So fast, and you will receive from the Lord what you ask.” So I fasted for one day, and that same night a young man appeared to me. He said to me, “Why do you keep asking for revelations in your prayers? Take care, or by asking so much you may harm your flesh. These revelations are enough for you. Are you able to see mightier revelations than those you have seen?”

I answered him, “Sir, I ask only this: that the revelation about the three forms of the old woman may be complete.” He answered me, “How long will all of you be without understanding? It is your double-mindedness that leaves you without understanding, and your not having your heart turned toward the Lord.” I answered him again, “But from you, sir, we shall learn these things more exactly.”

“Hear about the forms you are asking about,” he said. “In the first vision, why did she appear to you as an old woman, sitting in a chair? Because your spirit is old and already withered, and has no power, because of your softness and your double-mindedness. Old people, who no longer have any hope of renewal, expect nothing but their falling asleep. In the same way you, made soft by the affairs of daily life, gave yourselves up to listlessness and did not cast your cares upon the Lord. Your mind was broken, and you grew old in your griefs.” I said, “Then why was she sitting in a chair? I would like to know, sir.” He said, “Because everyone who is weak sits in a chair on account of his weakness, so that the weakness of his body may be supported. There you have the meaning of the first vision.

“In the second vision you saw her standing, with a face younger and more cheerful than before, but with her flesh and her hair old. Hear this parable also,” he said. “When an old man has already given up hope for himself, because of his weakness and his poverty, he looks for nothing but the last day of his life. Then suddenly an inheritance is left to him. He hears of it and rises up, and in his great joy he puts on strength. He no longer lies down, but stands. His spirit, already ruined by his former deeds, is renewed. He sits no longer, but bears himself with courage. So it was with you. You heard the revelation the Lord revealed to you, that he had compassion on you and renewed your spirits. You put away your softness, strength came to you, and you were made powerful in the faith. The Lord saw you made strong, and he rejoiced. That is why he showed you the building of the tower, and he will show you other things also, if with all your heart you keep peace among yourselves.

“In the third vision you saw her younger, and beautiful, and cheerful, and her form was beautiful. When good news comes to someone who is grieving, at once he forgets his former griefs. He thinks of nothing but the news he has heard. From then on he is made strong for what is good, and his spirit is renewed by the joy he has received. So you also have received a renewal of your spirits by seeing these good things. And as for your seeing her seated on a bench: the position is a strong one, because the bench has four feet and stands strong. For the world too is upheld by four elements. So those who have repented will be wholly young and firmly founded, those who have repented with all their heart. Now you have the revelation in full. Ask nothing more about revelation. But if anything is needed, it will be revealed to you.”
orientation: The old woman, who is the Church, meets Hermas in his field and shows him a great tower being built on water. She explains the tower, its stones and the seven women around it, and afterward a young man explains why she has looked younger each time Hermas has seen her.

title: The Beast as a Type of the Coming Tribulation
english: Brothers, this is the vision I saw twenty days after the earlier vision had come to me. It was a foreshadowing of the tribulation that is coming.
I was going out to the country along the Campanian road. The place is about ten furlongs from the public road, and it is easy going.

As I walked alone, I asked the Lord to complete the revelations and the visions he had shown me through his holy Church. I asked that he would make me strong and give repentance to his servants who had stumbled. I asked this so that his great and glorious name might be glorified, because he had counted me worthy to be shown his wonders.

While I was glorifying him and giving him thanks, something like the sound of a voice answered me, “Do not be double-minded, Hermas.” I began to turn this over within myself. I said, “Why should I be double-minded, when the Lord has set me on so firm a foundation and I have seen glorious things?”

I went on a little farther, brothers, and look, I saw a cloud of dust that seemed to reach the sky. I began to say to myself, “Could that be cattle coming, and raising the dust?” It was about a furlong away from me.

The cloud of dust grew greater and greater, and I suspected that it was something divine. The sun shone out a little, and look, I saw an enormous beast, like some sea monster, and fiery locusts were coming out of its mouth. The beast was about a hundred feet long, and its head looked like earthenware.
I began to weep, and to beg the Lord to rescue me from it. Then I remembered the word I had heard: “Do not be double-minded, Hermas.”

So, brothers, I put on the faith of the Lord and called to mind the great things he had taught me. I took courage and went to face the beast. And the beast came rushing on with such a noise that it could have laid a city waste.
I came close to it, and that huge sea monster stretched itself out on the ground. It did nothing but put out its tongue, and it did not stir at all until I had passed it by.
The beast had four colors on its head: black, then the color of fire and blood, then gold, then white.

After I had passed the beast and gone on about thirty feet, look, a virgin came to meet me. She was adorned as though she were coming out of a bridal chamber, all in white and with white sandals. She was veiled as far as the forehead, with a headdress for her covering, and her hair was white.
From the earlier visions I knew that she was the Church, and I grew more cheerful. She greeted me and said, “Greetings to you, man.” I greeted her in return: “Lady, greetings.”
She answered me, “Did nothing meet you?” I said to her, “Lady, a beast so huge that it could destroy whole peoples. But by the power of the Lord and by his great compassion I escaped it.”

“You did well to escape it,” she said, “because you cast your care upon God and opened your heart to the Lord. You believed that you can be saved by nothing except the great and glorious name. For this reason the Lord sent his angel, the one who is over the beasts, whose name is Thegri, and shut the beast’s mouth so that it would do you no harm. You have escaped a great tribulation because of your faith, and because you saw so huge a beast and were not double-minded.

“Go, then, and tell the Lord’s elect of his mighty works. Tell them that this beast is a foreshadowing of the great tribulation that is to come. If, then, you prepare yourselves ahead of time and repent to the Lord with your whole heart, you will be able to escape it. You will be able to, if your heart becomes pure and unblemished and you serve the Lord blamelessly for the rest of the days of your life. Cast your cares upon the Lord, and he will set them right.

“Believe the Lord, you double-minded: he can do all things. He turns his wrath away from you, and he sends scourges upon you who are double-minded. Woe to those who hear these words and refuse to heed them. It would have been better for them not to have been born.”
I asked her about the four colors that the beast had on its head. She answered me, “Again you are too curious about such things.” “Yes, lady,” I said. “Make known to me what they are.”
“Listen,” she said. “The black is this world in which you live.
“The color of fire and blood means that this world must perish by blood and fire.

“The golden part is you, who have fled from this world. For just as gold is tested by fire and becomes useful, so you also are being tested, you who live among them. Those of you who endure, and are put through the fire by them, will be made pure. Just as gold casts off its dross, so you too will cast off all grief and anguish. You will be made pure, and you will be useful for the building of the tower.
“The white part is the age to come, in which the elect of God will live. For those whom God has chosen for eternal life will be spotless and pure.

“So you must not stop speaking in the hearing of the saints. All of you have this too: the foreshadowing of the great tribulation that is coming. But if you are willing, it will be nothing. Remember what was written before.”
When she had said these things she went away, and I did not see where she went, for a cloud came. And I turned around in fear, thinking that the beast was coming.
orientation: Hermas tells his fellow believers about a vision he had on a country road outside Rome, twenty days after the last one. He meets a huge beast that stands for the coming tribulation, and then the Church, who earlier appeared as an old woman and now comes dressed as a bride.

title: The Shepherd arrives and commands Hermas to write
english: After I had prayed at home and sat down on my bed, a man came in, glorious to look at and dressed as a shepherd. He had a white goatskin wrapped around him, a bag on his shoulders, and a staff in his hand. He greeted me, and I greeted him in return.
At once he sat down beside me and said, “I have been sent by the most revered angel to live with you for the rest of the days of your life.”

I thought he had come to tempt me, and I said to him, “And who are you? For I know the one to whom I was handed over.” He said to me, “Do you not recognize me?” “No,” I said. “I am the Shepherd,” he said, “the one to whom you were handed over.”

While he was still speaking, his appearance changed, and I recognized him. He was the one to whom I had been handed over. At once I was thrown into confusion. Fear seized me, and I was utterly broken with grief, because I had answered him so wickedly and so foolishly.

But he answered me, “Do not be confused. Be strong in my commandments, which I am about to give you. For I was sent,” he said, “to show you again everything you saw before, the main points that are helpful for you all. First of all, write down my commandments and the parables. The rest you shall write just as I show you. This is why,” he said, “I command you to write the commandments and parables first: so that you may have them at hand to read and be able to keep them.”
So I wrote down the commandments and parables, just as he commanded me.

So then, if you hear them and keep them, if you walk in them and carry them out with a pure heart, you will receive from the Lord all that he promised you. But if you hear them and do not repent, but go on adding to your sins, you will receive the opposite from the Lord. All these things the Shepherd, the angel of repentance, commanded me to write just so.
orientation: Hermas is at home after prayer when a man dressed as a shepherd comes in. He is the angel of repentance, the Shepherd who gives the book its name, and he tells Hermas to write down the commandments and parables that follow.

title: First commandment: faith in the one God
english: “First of all, believe that God is one. He created all things and set them in order. He made all things come to be out of what was not. He contains all things, and he alone is uncontained.

“So believe in him and fear him, and, fearing him, be self-controlled. Keep these things, and you will cast all wickedness away from yourself and put on every virtue of righteousness, and you will live to God, if you keep this commandment.”
orientation: The Shepherd, the angel of repentance, now speaks. He gives Hermas the first of twelve commandments: believe in the one God who made all things, fear him, and practice self-control.

title: Simplicity and avoiding slander
english: The Shepherd said to me, “Hold to simplicity and be innocent, and you will be like little children, who do not know the wickedness that destroys human life.

“First, slander no one, and take no pleasure in listening to a slanderer. Otherwise you, the listener, will also be guilty of the slanderer’s sin, if you believe the slander you hear. For once you believe it, you too will hold something against your brother. In this way, then, you will be guilty of the slanderer’s sin.
“Slander is evil. It is a restless demon, never at peace, always living amid divisions. So keep away from it, and things will always go well between you and everyone.

“Put on reverence. In reverence there is nothing evil to stumble over. Everything is smooth and cheerful. Do what is good, and from the fruit of your labor, which God gives you, give with simplicity to all who are in need. Do not hesitate over whom you should give to and whom you should not. Give to all, for God wants everyone to be given a share of his own gifts.

“Those who receive will give an account to God of why they took and for what purpose. Those who take because they are hard pressed will not be judged. But those who take under false pretenses will pay the penalty.

“So the giver is guiltless. For he received from the Lord a ministry to carry out, and he carried it out with simplicity, making no distinction about whom to give to and whom not. So this ministry, carried out with simplicity, became glorious in the sight of God. Whoever serves with simplicity in this way will live to God.
“Keep this commandment, then, as I have spoken it to you, so that your repentance and the repentance of your household may be found in simplicity, and your innocence pure and undefiled.”
orientation: The Shepherd gives Hermas the second commandment. It is about simplicity: slander no one, and give to all who are in need without picking and choosing.

title: Love truth and speak no lie
english: Again the Shepherd said to me, “Love truth, and let everything that comes from your mouth be truth, so that the spirit God has made to dwell in this flesh may be found true by all people. In this way the Lord who dwells in you will be glorified. For the Lord is true in every word, and with him there is no lie.

“So those who lie reject the Lord. They become defrauders of the Lord, for they do not give back to him the deposit they received. They received from him a spirit that does not lie. If they give it back a lying spirit, they have defiled the Lord’s commandment and become defrauders.”
When I heard this, I wept bitterly. Seeing me weep, he said, “Why are you weeping?”
“Because, sir,” I said, “I do not know whether I can be saved.”
“Why?” he said.

“Because, sir,” I said, “never yet in my life have I spoken a true word. I have always spoken craftily with everyone, and I passed my lie off as truth before all people. No one ever contradicted me. My word was believed. How then, sir,” I said, “can I live, after doing these things?”

“Your thinking is right and true,” he said. “For as God’s servant you ought to have walked in truth. An evil conscience ought not to have dwelt with the spirit of truth, and you ought not to have brought grief upon the spirit that is revered and true.”
“Never, sir,” I said, “have I heard such words so exactly.”

“Well, now you hear them,” he said. “Keep them, so that even the lies you told before in your business dealings may become trustworthy, once these words are found true. For those too can become trustworthy. If you keep these things, and from now on speak nothing but truth, you will be able to gain life for yourself. And whoever hears this commandment and keeps away from lying, that most wicked thing, will live to God.”
orientation: The Shepherd gives Hermas the third commandment: love truth and tell no lies. Hermas weeps, because he has lied all his life in business.

title: The Commandment of Purity and the One Repentance
english: “I command you,” the Shepherd said, “to guard purity. Let no thought rise in your heart about another man’s wife, or about any sexual immorality, or about any evil things of that kind. For if you do this, you commit a great sin. But if you always keep your own wife in mind, you will never go wrong.

“For if this thought rises in your heart, you will go wrong. And if other things just as evil rise in it, you commit sin. For to a servant of God this thought is a great sin. And if anyone carries out this evil deed, he brings death upon himself.
“So watch yourself. Keep away from this thought. For where reverence dwells, lawlessness ought not to rise in the heart of a righteous man.”

I said to him, “Sir, allow me to ask you a few things.” “Speak,” he said. “Sir,” I said, “if a man has a wife who believes in the Lord, and he finds her in some act of adultery, does the husband sin if he goes on living with her?”

“As long as he does not know,” the Shepherd said, “he does not sin. But suppose the husband comes to know of her sin, and the wife does not repent but persists in her immorality. If the husband then goes on living with her, he becomes guilty of her sin and a partner in her adultery.”

“What then, sir,” I said, “is the husband to do, if the wife persists in this passion?” “Let him divorce her,” he said, “and let the husband remain by himself. But if he divorces his wife and marries another, he too commits adultery.”
“If then, sir,” I said, “after the wife has been divorced, she repents and wants to return to her own husband, will she not be taken back?”

“Yes indeed,” he said. “If the husband does not take her back, he sins and brings a great sin upon himself. The one who has sinned and repents must be taken back, but not many times. For the servants of God have one repentance. So, for the sake of repentance, the husband ought not to marry. This rule holds for wife and husband alike.

“Adultery,” he said, “is not only when someone defiles his flesh. Whoever does the kind of things the nations do also commits adultery. So if anyone persists in such deeds and does not repent, keep away from him and do not live with him. Otherwise you too have a share in his sin.
“This is why you were commanded to remain by yourselves, whether husband or wife. For in such cases there can be repentance.

“So I am not giving an excuse,” he said, “for this thing to be done. I speak so that the one who has sinned may sin no more. As for his former sin, there is one who is able to give healing, for he is the one who has authority over all things.”

I asked him again, “Since the Lord has counted me worthy to have you dwell with me always, bear with a few more words from me. For I understand nothing, and my heart has been hardened by my former deeds. Give me understanding, for I am very foolish and grasp nothing at all.”

He answered me, “I am set over repentance, and I give understanding to all who repent. Or do you not think,” he said, “that to repent is itself understanding? To repent,” he said, “is great understanding. For the one who has sinned understands that he has done evil before the Lord. The deed he did rises in his heart, and he repents and no longer does evil. Instead he does good lavishly, and he humbles his own soul and torments it, because he sinned. You see, then, that repentance is great understanding.”
“That is why, sir,” I said, “I question you so exactly about everything. First, because I am a sinner, I ask so that I may know what works I must do to live. For my sins are many and of many kinds.”
“You will live,” he said, “if you keep my commandments and walk in them. And whoever hears these commandments and keeps them will live to God.”

“Sir,” I said, “I will ask one thing more.” “Speak,” he said. “Sir,” I said, “I have heard from certain teachers that there is no other repentance except the one when we went down into the water and received forgiveness of our former sins.”
He said to me, “You have heard rightly, for so it is. The one who has received forgiveness of sins ought to sin no more, but to live in purity.

“But since you ask about everything so exactly, I will make this clear to you as well. I do not say it to give an excuse to those who are going to believe, or to those who have now come to believe in the Lord. For those who have now believed, or are going to believe, have no repentance for sins. What they have is forgiveness of their former sins.

“So it was for those who were called before these days that the Lord appointed repentance. For the Lord knows the heart, and he knows all things before they happen. He knew the weakness of human beings and the great cunning of the devil. He knew that the devil would do some evil to the servants of God and deal wickedly with them.
“So the Lord, who is full of compassion, had compassion on what he had made and appointed this repentance. And the authority over this repentance was given to me.

“But I tell you,” he said, “after that great and solemn calling, if anyone is tempted by the devil and sins, he has one repentance. But if he sins again and again and repents, it is of no use to such a person, for he will live only with difficulty.”

I said to him, “I was brought to life when I heard these things from you so exactly. For I know that if I add no more to my sins, I will be saved.” “You will be saved,” he said, “and so will all who do these things.”

I asked him again, “Sir, since you bear with me this once, make this clear to me as well.” “Speak,” he said. “Sir,” I said, “if a wife, or again a husband, falls asleep in death, and one of them marries, does the one who marries sin?”
“He does not sin,” the Shepherd said. “But if he remains by himself, he gains greater honor for himself and great glory with the Lord. Yet even if he marries, he does not sin.

“So guard purity and reverence, and you will live to God. Everything I am telling you, and everything I am going to tell you, keep from now on, from the day you were handed over to me, and I will dwell in your house.
“For your former transgressions there will be forgiveness, if you keep my commandments. And there will be forgiveness for all, if they keep these commandments of mine and walk in this purity.”
orientation: The Shepherd gives Hermas the fourth commandment, on purity. Hermas asks about a wife who is unfaithful, about whether there is repentance after baptism, and about marrying again after a husband or wife has died.

title: Patience and anger as rival spirits
english: “Be patient and understanding,” the Shepherd said, “and you will master all evil deeds and do all righteousness.

“For if you are patient, the Holy Spirit that dwells in you will be clean, not darkened by another spirit, an evil one. It will dwell in a wide and open place. It will rejoice and be glad together with the vessel in which it dwells, and it will serve God with great cheerfulness, for all is well within it.

“But if any anger comes near, the Holy Spirit, which is tender, is at once pressed for room. It does not have a clean place, and it seeks to leave that place. For it is choked by the evil spirit. It has no room to serve the Lord as it wishes, because it is defiled by the anger. For the Lord dwells in patience, but the devil dwells in anger.
“So when both spirits dwell in the same place, it is unprofitable and evil for the person in whom they dwell.

“For if you take a very little wormwood and pour it into a jar of honey, is not all the honey spoiled? Is not so much honey ruined by the least bit of wormwood? Does the wormwood not destroy the sweetness of the honey, so that it no longer finds the same favor with its master, because it has been made bitter and has lost its use? But if the wormwood is not put into the honey, the honey is found sweet and is useful to its master.

“You see that patience is sweeter by far than honey and is useful to the Lord, and he dwells in it. But anger is bitter and useless. So if anger is mixed with patience, the patience is defiled, and its prayer is no longer useful to God.”

“Sir,” I said, “I would like to know how anger works, so that I may guard myself against it.” “Indeed,” he said, “if you do not guard yourself against it, you and your household, you have lost all your hope. But guard yourself against it, for I am with you. And all who repent with their whole heart will keep away from it, for I will be with them and will keep them safe. For they have all been justified by the most revered angel.

“Hear now,” he said, “how anger works: how evil it is, how it overthrows my servants by its working, and how it leads them astray from righteousness. It does not lead astray those who are full of faith, nor can it work on them, because my power is with them. But it does lead astray those who are empty and double-minded.

“When it sees such people living in calm, it forces its way into the heart of one of them. Then, out of nothing, the man or the woman turns bitter over everyday affairs, or over food, or some trifle, or some friend, or giving or receiving, or foolish things of that kind. For all these things are foolish and empty and senseless, and unprofitable for the servants of God.

“But patience is great and strong. It has a sturdy power that flourishes in a wide and open space. It is cheerful, glad, and free from care. It glorifies the Lord at all times, has nothing bitter in itself, and remains always gentle and quiet. This patience, then, dwells with those whose faith is whole.

“Anger, though, is first of all foolish, fickle, and senseless. Then from senselessness comes bitterness, from bitterness rage, from rage wrath, and from wrath fury. Then this fury, made up of so many evils, becomes a great sin that cannot be healed.
“For when these spirits dwell in one vessel, where the Holy Spirit also dwells, that vessel cannot hold them. It overflows.
“So the tender Spirit, which is not used to dwelling with an evil spirit or with harshness, withdraws from such a person and seeks to dwell with gentleness and quietness.

“Then, when it has left the person in whom it dwells, that person becomes empty of the righteous Spirit. From then on he is filled with the evil spirits and is unsettled in everything he does. The evil spirits drag him this way and that, and he is made wholly blind to good thinking. This, then, is what happens to all who are given to anger.

“So keep away from anger, that most evil spirit. Put on patience, and stand against anger and bitterness, and you will be found in the company of the reverence that the Lord loves. See, then, that you never neglect this commandment. For if you master this commandment, you will be able to keep the other commandments as well, the ones I am about to give you. Be strong in them and filled with power, and let all who want to walk in them be filled with power.”
orientation: The Shepherd gives Hermas the fifth commandment, on patience and anger. He pictures them as two spirits that cannot share one home: when anger moves in, the Holy Spirit is crowded out.

title: The two angels and their works
english: “In the first commandment,” the Shepherd said, “I commanded you to guard faith and fear and self-control.” “Yes, sir,” I said. “But now,” he said, “I want to show you their powers as well, so that you may understand what power each of them has, and how it works. For their workings are twofold. They bear on what is righteous and on what is unrighteous.

“So put your faith in what is righteous, and put no faith in what is unrighteous. For what is righteous has a straight way, but what is unrighteous has a crooked one. As for you, walk in the straight and level way, and leave the crooked way alone. For the crooked way has no beaten paths. It is trackless ground, full of stumbling blocks, and it is rough and thorny. So it does harm to those who walk in it. But those who walk in the straight way walk smoothly and without stumbling, for it is neither rough nor thorny. You see, then, that it is better to walk in this way.”

“Sir,” I said, “I am glad to walk in this way.” “You will walk in it,” he said, “and whoever turns to the Lord with a whole heart will walk in it. Now hear,” he said, “about faith. There are two angels with a person, one of righteousness and one of wickedness.”
“How then, sir,” I said, “am I to know their workings, since both angels dwell with me?”

“Listen,” he said, “and you will understand them. The angel of righteousness is tender and modest, gentle and quiet. So when this angel rises in your heart, at once he speaks with you about righteousness, about purity, about reverence, about contentment, about every righteous deed and every glorious virtue. When all these things rise in your heart, know that the angel of righteousness is with you. These, then, are the works of the angel of righteousness. So put your faith in him and in his works.

“Now look at the works of the angel of wickedness as well. First of all, he is angry and bitter and senseless, and his works are evil. They overthrow the servants of God. So when this angel rises in your heart, know him by his works.”

“Sir,” I said, “I do not know how I am to recognize him.” “Listen,” he said. “When some anger comes over you, or bitterness, know that he is in you. Then comes the desire for many activities, and extravagance in many kinds of food and strong drink, in much carousing, and in foods that are varied and not needed. Then come desires for women, and greed, and great pride, and boastfulness, and everything close to these and like them. So when these things rise in your heart, know that the angel of wickedness is in you.

“So when you recognize his works, draw away from him and put no faith in him at all, because his works are evil and unprofitable for the servants of God. Now you have the workings of both angels. Understand them, and put your faith in the angel of righteousness. But draw away from the angel of wickedness, because his teaching is evil in every deed. For if a man is faithful, and the thought of this angel rises in his heart, that man, or that woman, must commit some sin. And again, if a man or a woman is very wicked, and the works of the angel of righteousness rise in that person’s heart, then of necessity that person must do something good.

“You see, then,” he said, “that it is good to follow the angel of righteousness and to renounce the angel of wickedness. This commandment makes plain what concerns faith, so that you may put your faith in the works of the angel of righteousness, and by doing them you will live to God. But believe that the works of the angel of wickedness are dangerous. So by not doing them you will live to God.”
orientation: The Shepherd gives Hermas the sixth commandment. Two angels stay with every person, one of righteousness and one of wickedness, and Hermas learns to tell them apart by what each stirs up in the heart.

title: The Two Fears
english: “Fear the Lord,” the Shepherd said, “and keep his commandments. If you keep the commandments of God, you will be powerful in every deed, and what you do will be beyond compare. For when you fear the Lord, you will do everything well. This is the fear you must have in order to be saved.

“But do not fear the devil. For if you fear the Lord, you will master the devil, because there is no power in him. One who has no power inspires no fear. But one who has glorious power inspires fear as well. For everyone who has power is feared, and the one who has no power is despised by all.
“But do fear the works of the devil, because they are evil. If you fear the Lord, you will not do them. You will keep away from them.

“So there are two kinds of fear. If you want to do evil, fear the Lord, and you will not do it. If, on the other hand, you want to do good, fear the Lord, and you will do it. So the fear of the Lord is strong and great and glorious. Fear the Lord, then, and you will live to him. And all who fear him and keep his commandments will live to God.”

“Sir,” I said, “why did you say of those who keep his commandments, ‘They will live to God’?” “Because,” he said, “all creation fears the Lord, but it does not keep his commandments. So life with God belongs to those who fear him and keep his commandments. But those who do not keep his commandments have no life in him.”
orientation: The Shepherd gives Hermas the seventh commandment: fear the Lord and keep his commandments, but do not fear the devil, who has no power.

title: Two kinds of self-control: from evil, not from good
english: “I told you,” the Shepherd said, “that the things God has created are twofold. Self-control is twofold as well. For there are some things from which we must hold back, and some from which we must not.”

“Make known to me, sir,” I said, “from what things we must hold back, and from what things we must not.” “Listen,” he said. “Hold back from evil, and do not do it. But do not hold back from good. Do it. For if you hold back from doing good, you commit a great sin. But if you hold back from doing evil, you do a great act of righteousness. So hold back from all wickedness, and do what is good.”

“Sir,” I said, “what kinds of wickedness must we hold back from?” “Listen,” he said. “From adultery and sexual immorality. From lawless drunkenness. From wicked luxury. From much food, and the extravagance of wealth, and boasting, and haughtiness, and pride. From lying and slander and hypocrisy, from bearing grudges, and from all blasphemy.
“These deeds are the most evil of all in human life. So the servant of God must hold back from these deeds. For whoever does not hold back from them cannot live to God. Now hear what follows them.”

“Sir,” I said, “are there still more evil deeds?” “Yes, many more,” he said, “from which the servant of God must hold back: theft, falsehood, fraud, false witness, greed, evil desire, deceit, conceit, boastfulness, and everything like these.

“Do you not think these are evil?” “Very evil indeed,” I said, “for the servants of God.” “From all of these,” he said, “the one who serves God must hold back. So hold back from all of them, so that you may live to God and be enrolled among those who hold back from them. These, then, are the things from which you must hold back.
“Now hear,” he said, “the things from which you must not hold back, but which you must do. Do not hold back from good. Do it.”

“Sir,” I said, “show me the power of the good things as well, so that I may walk in them and serve them, and by doing them can be saved.” “Then hear,” he said, “the works of goodness too, which you must do, and from which you must not hold back.

“First of all: faith, fear of the Lord, love, harmony, words of righteousness, truth, endurance. Nothing in human life is better than these. If anyone keeps them and does not hold back from them, he becomes blessed in his life.

“Then hear what follows these: to serve widows, to visit orphans and those in need, to rescue the servants of God from hardship, and to be hospitable, for in hospitality good is sometimes done. To oppose no one, to be quiet, to be poorer than everyone else. To respect the aged, to practice righteousness, to preserve brotherhood, to bear insult, to be patient, to hold no grudge. To comfort those who are weary in soul. Not to cast off those who have stumbled from the faith, but to turn them back and put them in good heart. To admonish sinners, not to press hard on debtors or the needy, and whatever else is like these.
“Do these seem good to you?” he said. “Sir,” I said, “what could be better than these?” “Then walk in them,” he said, “and do not hold back from them, and you will live to God.

“So keep this commandment. If you do good and do not hold back from it, you will live to God, and all who do the same will live to God. And again, if you do not do evil, but hold back from it, you will live to God. And all will live to God who keep these commandments and walk in them.”
orientation: The Shepherd gives Hermas the eighth commandment, on self-control. Self-control here means holding back: hold back from evil, but never hold back from good.

title: The Ninth Commandment: Cast Off Double-Mindedness and Ask in Faith
english: The Shepherd said to me, “Rid yourself of double-mindedness. Do not be double-minded at all about asking God for anything, saying to yourself, ‘How can I ask anything of the Lord and receive it, when I have sinned so greatly against him?’ Do not reason this way. Turn to the Lord with your whole heart and ask of him without doubting, and you will know his great compassion: he will never abandon you, but will fulfill the request of your soul.

“For God is not like human beings, who hold grudges. He holds no grudge, and he has compassion on what he has made. So cleanse your heart of all the empty things of this age, and of the words I spoke of just now, and ask of the Lord. You will receive everything, and you will lack nothing that you ask for, if you ask of the Lord without doubting.

“But if you doubt in your heart, you will receive none of your requests. For those who doubt God are the double-minded, and they obtain none of their requests at all. But those who are whole in the faith ask for everything, trusting in the Lord, and they receive, because they ask without doubting and are not double-minded in anything. For every double-minded man, unless he repents, will be saved only with difficulty.

“So cleanse your heart of double-mindedness and put on faith, because faith is strong. Believe God, that you will receive all the requests you make. And if ever you ask the Lord for something and are slow to receive it, do not be double-minded because you did not quickly receive the request of your soul. For surely it is because of some trial, or some transgression you do not know of, that you are slow to receive your request.

“So do not stop making the request of your soul, and you will receive it. But if you grow weary and become double-minded as you ask, blame yourself, and not the one who gives to you. Watch out for this double-mindedness. It is wicked and without understanding, and it uproots many from the faith, even those who are very faithful and strong. For this double-mindedness is a daughter of the devil, and it does great wickedness to the servants of God.

“So despise double-mindedness and master it in everything. Put on the faith that is strong and powerful. For faith promises all things and brings all things to completion. But double-mindedness has no confidence in itself, and it fails in every work it undertakes. You see, then,” he said, “that faith is from above, from the Lord, and has great power. But double-mindedness is an earthly spirit from the devil, and it has no power. So serve faith, which has power, and keep away from double-mindedness, which has none, and you will live to God. And all who are of this mind will live to God.”
orientation: The Shepherd gives Hermas the ninth commandment: put away double-mindedness and ask God for what you need with full faith.

title: Grief, the sister of double-mindedness and anger
english: “Rid yourself of grief,” the Shepherd said, “for grief too is a sister of double-mindedness and of anger.”

“Sir,” I said, “how is grief a sister of these? Anger seems to me one thing, double-mindedness another, and grief another.” “You are without understanding, man,” he said. “Do you not see that grief is more wicked than all the spirits, and most terrible for the servants of God? More than all the spirits it ruins a person and wears out the Holy Spirit, and then again it saves.”
“Sir,” I said, “I am without understanding, and I do not understand these parables. How grief can wear out and then again save, I do not grasp.”

“Listen,” he said. “There are those who have never searched for the truth or inquired about divinity. They have only believed, and they are mixed up in business and wealth and friendships among the nations and the many other affairs of this age. All who are devoted to these things fail to grasp the parables of divinity. For they are darkened by these activities, and ruined, and they become barren.

“Good vineyards, when they are neglected, are made barren by thorns and weeds of many kinds. In the same way, people who have believed and then fall into these many activities already named find their minds led astray, and they grasp nothing at all about righteousness. Even when they hear about divinity and truth, their mind is taken up with their own business, and they grasp nothing at all.

“But there are those who have the fear of God, who search into divinity and truth and have their heart set toward the Lord. They quickly grasp and understand everything that is said to them, because they have the fear of the Lord in themselves. For where the Lord dwells, there is much understanding as well. So cling to the Lord, and you will understand and grasp everything.
“Hear then, foolish man,” he said, “how grief wears out the Holy Spirit and then again saves.
“When the double-minded man takes some work in hand and fails in it because of his double-mindedness, this grief enters into the man. It grieves the Holy Spirit and wears it out.

“Then again, when anger clings to a man over some matter and he becomes very bitter, grief again enters the heart of the man who was angry. He is grieved at the deed he has done, and he repents, because he did evil.

“So this grief seems to hold salvation, because the man who did evil repented. Both actions, then, grieve the Spirit. Double-mindedness grieves the Spirit because it did not succeed in what it set out to do, and anger grieves the Spirit because it did what is evil. So both are grievous to the Holy Spirit, double-mindedness and anger.
“So rid yourself of grief, and do not press hard upon the Holy Spirit that dwells in you, or it may appeal to God and depart from you.
“For the Spirit of God that was given to this flesh does not bear grief or anguish.
“So put on cheerfulness, which always finds favor with God and is welcome to him, and take your delight in it. For every cheerful man does good things and thinks good things and despises grief.

“But the grieving man always does wickedly. First, he does wickedly because he grieves the Holy Spirit, which was given to man as a cheerful Spirit. Second, by grieving the Holy Spirit he works lawlessness, for he neither prays nor confesses to the Lord. For the prayer of a grieving man never has the power to rise to the altar of God.”

“Why,” I said, “does the prayer of the grieving man not rise to the altar?” “Because,” he said, “grief sits in his heart. So the grief is mixed with the prayer, and it does not let the prayer rise pure to the altar. For vinegar and wine, mixed together, do not have the same pleasant taste. In the same way, when grief is mixed with the Holy Spirit, the prayer is not the same.
“So cleanse yourself of this wicked grief, and you will live to God. And all will live to God who cast grief away from themselves and put on all cheerfulness.”
orientation: The Shepherd gives Hermas the tenth commandment: put away grief and put on cheerfulness. He explains how grief can wear out the Holy Spirit, and how the grief that leads to repentance can save.

title: True and false prophets
english: The Shepherd showed me some people sitting on a bench, and another man sitting on a chair. He said to me, “Do you see the people sitting on the bench?” “I see them, sir,” I said. “They are faithful,” he said, “and the man sitting on the chair is a false prophet, who destroys the mind of the servants of God. But it is the mind of the double-minded that he destroys, not the mind of the faithful.

“So these double-minded people come to him as they would to a soothsayer, and they ask him what is going to happen to them. And that false prophet has no power of a divine Spirit in him. He speaks with them according to their questions and according to their wicked desires, and he fills their souls just as they themselves wish.

“For he is empty himself, and he gives empty answers to empty people. Whatever he is asked, he answers to match the emptiness of the person. Yet he does speak some true words. For the devil fills him with his own spirit, to see whether he can break any of the righteous.

“So all who are strong in the faith of the Lord, who have put on the truth, do not cling to such spirits. They keep away from them. But all who are double-minded, who are forever repenting, turn to soothsaying, just as the nations do, and they bring a greater sin upon themselves by their idolatry. For anyone who consults a false prophet about any matter is an idolater, empty of the truth, and senseless.

“For no spirit given by God is consulted. It has the power of divinity and speaks everything of its own accord, because it is from above, from the power of the divine Spirit. But the spirit that is consulted, and that speaks according to people’s desires, is earthly and fickle, and has no power. It does not speak at all unless it is consulted.”

“How then, sir,” I said, “will a person know which of them is a prophet and which is a false prophet?” “Hear,” he said, “about both kinds of prophet. As I am about to tell you, so you shall test the prophet and the false prophet. Test the man who has the divine Spirit by his life.

“First, the one who has the Spirit from above is gentle and quiet and humble. He keeps away from all wickedness and from the empty desire of this age. He makes himself needier than everyone else. He gives no answer to anyone when he is consulted, and he does not speak in private. The Holy Spirit does not speak when a man wants to speak. He speaks at the time when God wants him to speak.

“So the man who has the divine Spirit comes into a gathering of righteous men who have faith in the divine Spirit, and that gathering makes its prayer to God. Then the angel of the prophetic Spirit who is assigned to him fills the man. And the man, filled with the Holy Spirit, speaks to the multitude as the Lord wills.
“In this way, then, the Spirit of divinity will be made plain. Such, then, is the power of the Spirit of the Lord’s divinity.

“Now hear,” he said, “about the spirit that is earthly and empty, that has no power but is foolish. First, the man who seems to have a spirit exalts himself and wants to have the chief seat. At once he is brash and shameless and full of talk. He lives among many luxuries and many other deceits, and he takes pay for his prophecy. If he is not paid, he does not prophesy. Can a divine Spirit take pay and prophesy? It is not possible for a prophet of God to do this. No, the spirit of such prophets is earthly.

“Next, he never comes near a gathering of righteous men. He shuns them. He clings to the double-minded and the empty, and prophesies to them in a corner. He deceives them, saying everything emptily, to suit their desires. For it is empty people he is answering. For an empty vessel set among other empty vessels is not broken. They agree with one another.

“But when he comes into a gathering full of righteous men who have the Spirit of divinity, and they make their prayer, that man is emptied. The earthly spirit flees from him in fear. The man is struck dumb and is altogether shattered, unable to say anything.

“For suppose you stack wine or oil in a storeroom and set an empty jar among them, and later you want to clear the storeroom out. You will find that jar empty, just as you set it there. So it is with the empty prophets. When they come among the spirits of righteous men, they are found to be just what they were when they came.
“You now have the life of both kinds of prophet. So test by his deeds and his life the man who says that he bears the Spirit.
“As for you, put your faith in the Spirit that comes from God and has power. But put no faith at all in the earthly and empty spirit, because there is no power in it. For it comes from the devil.

“Hear, then, the parable I am about to tell you. Take a stone and throw it at the sky, and see whether you can touch the sky. Or again, take a water squirt and squirt it at the sky, and see whether you can pierce the sky.”
“Sir,” I said, “how can these things be done? Both the things you have named are impossible.” “Just as these things cannot be done,” he said, “so the earthly spirits can do nothing, and are feeble.
