I said to him, “Sir, what am I to do here all alone?” “You are not alone,” he said, “for these virgins are with you.” “Then hand me over to them,” I said. The Shepherd called them to him and said to them, “I entrust this man to you until I come.” And he went away.
So I was alone with the virgins. They were all the more cheerful, and they were kind to me, above all the four who were the more glorious among them.

The virgins said to me, “The Shepherd is not coming here today.” “Then what am I to do?” I said. They said, “Wait for him until evening. If he comes, he will speak with you. But if he does not come, you will stay here with us until he does.”

I said to them, “I will wait for him until evening. But if he does not come, I will go home and come back in the morning.” But they answered me, “You were handed over to us. You cannot go away from us.”

“Then where am I to stay?” I said. They said, “You will sleep with us as a brother, and not as a husband. For you are our brother, and from now on we are going to dwell with you, for we love you very much.” But I was ashamed to stay with them.
Then the one who seemed to be first among them began to kiss me and embrace me. When the others saw her embracing me, they too began to kiss me, and to lead me around the tower, and to play with me.

And it was as if I had become a younger man, and I too began to play with them. For some of them were dancing in a ring, others were leaping in dance, and others were singing. But I kept silent and walked with them around the tower, and I was cheerful with them.
When evening came, I wanted to go home. But they would not let me go. They held me back. So I stayed the night with them, and I slept beside the tower.

For the virgins spread their linen tunics on the ground and made me lie down in the middle of them, and they did nothing at all but pray. And I prayed with them without ceasing, no less than they did. The virgins rejoiced that I was praying in this way. And I stayed there with the virgins until the next day, until the second hour.

Then the Shepherd arrived, and he said to the virgins, “You have not mistreated him in any way, have you?” “Ask him,” they said. I said to him, “Sir, I was glad to stay with them.” “What did you dine on?” he asked. “Sir,” I said, “I dined on the words of the Lord the whole night long.” “Did they receive you well?” he asked. “Yes, sir,” I said.

“Now,” said the Shepherd, “what do you want to hear first?” “Just as you showed it to me from the beginning, sir,” I said. “I ask you, sir, to make each thing clear to me as I question you.” “As you wish,” he said. “That is how I will explain it to you, and I will hide nothing at all from you.”

“First of all, sir,” I said, “make this clear to me. The rock and the gate: what are they?” “This rock and the gate are the Son of God,” he said. “Sir,” I said, “how is it that the rock is old, but the gate is new?” “Listen,” he said, “and understand, you who lack understanding.
“The Son of God is older than all his creation, so that he was the Father’s counselor in his creation. That is why the rock is old.” “But the gate, sir,” I said, “why is it new?”
“Because he was revealed in the last days, the days of the end,” he said. “That is why the gate was made new, so that those who are going to be saved may enter the kingdom of God through it.

“Did you see,” he said, “how the stones that came in through the gate were put into the building of the tower, while those that did not come in through it were cast back out to their own place?” “I saw it, sir,” I said. “In the same way,” he said, “no one will enter the kingdom of God unless he receives his holy name.

“For if you want to enter a certain city, and that city has a wall all around it and one gate, can you enter that city except through the gate it has?” “How could it be any other way, sir?” I said. “Then if you cannot enter the city except through the gate it has,” he said, “so too a person cannot enter the kingdom of God in any other way than through the name of his Son, whom he loves.

“Did you see the crowd that was building the tower?” he said. “I saw them, sir,” I said. “They are all glorious angels,” he said. “The Lord is walled around by them. But the gate is the Son of God. This is the one way in to the Lord. So no one will come in to him in any other way than through his Son.
“Did you see the six men,” he said, “and the glorious and great man in the middle of them, who walked around the tower and rejected the stones from the building?” “I saw them, sir,” I said.

“The glorious man is the Son of God,” he said, “and those six are the glorious angels who support him on the right and on the left. Not one of these glorious angels,” he said, “will come in to God without him. Whoever does not receive his name will not enter the kingdom of God.”
“And the tower,” I said, “what is it?” “This tower is the church,” he said.

“And these virgins, who are they?” I asked. “They are holy spirits,” he said, “and a person cannot be found in the kingdom of God unless these virgins clothe him with their garment. For if you receive the name alone, and do not receive the garment from them, it will do you no good. For these virgins are powers of the Son of God. If you wear the name but do not wear his power, you will be wearing his name in vain.

“As for the stones you saw cast out,” he said, “they wore the name, but they did not put on the clothing of the virgins.” “What kind of clothing do they have, sir?” I asked. “Their very names are their clothing,” he said. “Whoever wears the name of the Son of God ought to wear their names as well. For even the Son himself wears the names of these virgins.
“All the stones that you saw go into the building of the tower,” he said, “handed in by the virgins’ hands and remaining in the building, are clothed with the power of these virgins.

“That is why you see that the tower has become a single stone with the rock. So too those who have believed in the Lord through his Son, and are clothed with these spirits, will become one spirit and one body, and their clothes will be of one color. And those who wear the names of the virgins, people such as these, have their dwelling in the tower.”

“Then the stones that were cast out, sir,” I said, “why were they cast out? For they passed through the gate, and they were set in the building of the tower by the hands of the virgins.” “Since you care about everything,” he said, “and inquire so closely, hear about the stones that were cast out.

“They all received the name of the Son of God,” he said, “and they received the power of these virgins as well. So when they received these spirits, they were made strong, and they were with the servants of God. They had one spirit and one body and one garment, for they were of the same mind, and they practiced righteousness.

“Then, after a time, they were won over by the women you saw dressed in black, with their shoulders bare and their hair hanging loose, beautiful women. When they saw them, they desired them and put on their power, and they took off the garment and the power of the virgins.

“So they were cast out from the house of God and handed over to those women. But those who were not deceived by the beauty of these women remained in the house of God. There,” he said, “you have the explanation of those that were cast out.”

“What then, sir,” I said, “if these people, such as they are, repent? What if they cast off the desires of these women, and return to the virgins, and walk in their power and in their works? Will they not enter the house of God?”

“They will enter,” he said, “if they cast off the works of these women, and take up the power of the virgins, and walk in their works. That is the very reason there was a pause in the building: so that, if these people repent, they may go into the building of the tower. But if they do not repent, then others will go in, and these will be thrown out for good.”

For all these things I gave thanks to the Lord, because he had compassion on all who call on his name, and sent the angel of repentance to us who had sinned against him. He renewed our spirit, and when we were already ruined and had no hope of life, he made our life new.

“Now, sir,” I said, “make clear to me why the tower is not built on the ground, but on the rock and on the gate.” “Are you still foolish and without understanding?” he said. “Sir,” I said, “I have to ask you about everything, because I cannot grasp anything at all. For all these things are great and glorious, and hard for people to understand.”

“Listen,” he said. “The name of the Son of God is great, and nothing can contain it, and it carries the whole world. If, then, all creation is carried by the Son of God, what do you think of those who are called by him, who wear the name of the Son of God and walk in his commandments?

“Do you see, then, what kind of people he carries? Those who wear his name with their whole heart. So he himself has become their foundation, and he carries them gladly, because they are not ashamed to wear his name.”
“Sir,” I said, “tell me the names of the virgins, and of the women dressed in black.” “Hear the names of the stronger virgins,” he said, “the ones who stood at the corners.

“The first is Faith, the second Self-Control, the third Power, and the fourth Patience. The others, who stood between them, have these names: Simplicity, Innocence, Purity, Cheerfulness, Truth, Understanding, Harmony, Love. Whoever wears these names, and the name of the Son of God, will be able to enter the kingdom of God.

“Hear also,” he said, “the names of the women who have the black clothes. Of these, too, four are more powerful. The first is Unbelief, the second Lack of Self-Control, the third Disobedience, and the fourth Deceit. Those who follow them are called Grief, Wickedness, Licentiousness, Anger, Falsehood, Folly, Slander, Hatred. The servant of God who wears these names will see the kingdom of God, but he will not enter it.”

“And the stones, sir,” I said, “the ones from the deep that were fitted into the building, who are they?” “The first ones,” he said, “the ten that were set in the foundations, are the first generation. The twenty-five are the second generation, of righteous men. The thirty-five are prophets of God and his ministers. And the forty are apostles and teachers of the preaching of the Son of God.”
“Then why, sir,” I said, “did the virgins hand in these stones too for the building of the tower, after carrying them through the gate?”

“Because these were the first to wear these spirits,” he said, “and they never parted from one another at all, neither the spirits from the people nor the people from the spirits. The spirits stayed with them until they fell asleep. And if they had not had these spirits with them, they would not have been of use for the building of this tower.”

“Make one thing more clear to me, sir,” I said. “What more are you asking?” he said. “Why was it, sir,” I said, “that the stones came up from the deep and were set in the building of the tower, when they had worn these spirits?”
“They had to come up through water,” he said, “so that they might be made alive. For they could not enter the kingdom of God in any other way than by laying aside the deadness of their former life.

“So these too, who had fallen asleep, received the seal of the Son of God and entered the kingdom of God. For before a person wears the name of the Son of God,” he said, “he is dead. But when he receives the seal, he lays aside deadness and takes up life.

“The seal, then, is the water. They go down into the water dead, and they come up alive. So this seal was preached to them as well, and they made use of it, so that they might enter the kingdom of God.”

“Why, sir,” I said, “did the forty stones also come up from the deep with them, when they already had the seal?” “Because these apostles and teachers preached the name of the Son of God,” he said. “And when they had fallen asleep in the power and faith of the Son of God, they preached also to those who had fallen asleep before them. They themselves gave them the seal of the preaching.

“So they went down with them into the water, and came up again. But the apostles and teachers went down alive and came up alive. Those who had fallen asleep before them went down dead, but came up alive.

“Through the apostles and teachers, then, they were made alive, and came to know the name of the Son of God. That is why they also came up together with them, and were fitted together with them into the building of the tower, and were built in without being hewn. For they had fallen asleep in righteousness and in great purity. Only they did not have this seal. So you have the explanation of these things as well.” “I have it, sir,” I said.

“Now then, sir, tell me about the mountains. Why does each one look different from the next, and why are they varied?” “Listen,” he said. “These twelve mountains are the tribes that inhabit the whole world. And the Son of God was preached to them through the apostles.”

“But make clear to me, sir,” I said, “why the mountains are varied, each with a different appearance.” “Listen,” he said. “These twelve tribes that inhabit the whole world are twelve nations. And they are varied in their thinking and in their mind. As varied as the mountains you saw, so varied are the minds of these nations, and their thinking. And I will make clear to you the conduct of each one as well.”

“First, sir,” I said, “make this clear. The mountains are so varied. Why, then, when their stones were set in the building, did they become bright and of one color, like the stones that had come up from the deep?”

“Because all the nations that live under heaven,” he said, “when they heard and believed, were called by the name of the Son of God. So when they received the seal, they had one way of thinking and one mind. Their faith became one, and their love became one, and together with the name they wore the spirits of the virgins. That is why the building of the tower became one color, bright as the sun.

“But after they had come in together and become one body, some of them defiled themselves. They were thrown out of the family of the righteous, and became again what they had been before, or rather, even worse.”

“Sir,” I said, “how did they become worse, when they had come to know God?” “The one who does not know God and does evil,” he said, “has a certain punishment for his wickedness. But the one who has come to know God ought to do evil no longer. He ought to do good.

“So if the one who ought to do good does evil, does he not seem to do greater wickedness than the one who does not know God? That is why those who have not known God and do evil are condemned to death. But those who have known God and have seen his mighty works, and do evil, will be punished twice over, and they will die forever. In this way, then, the church of God will be cleansed.

“You saw how the stones were taken out of the tower, handed over to the evil spirits, and thrown out from there. And there will be one body of those who have been cleansed, just as the tower, after it was cleansed, became as though it were made of a single stone. So it will be with the church of God as well, after it has been cleansed, and the wicked have been cast out, and the hypocrites, and the blasphemers, and the double-minded, and those who do evil in all kinds of wickedness.

“After these have been cast out, the church of God will be one body, one way of thinking, one mind, one faith, one love. And then the Son of God will rejoice and be glad in them, when he has received his people back pure.”

“Sir,” I said, “all of this is great and glorious. Now make still more clear to me, sir, the power and the deeds of each one of the mountains, so that every soul that trusts in the Lord may hear, and glorify his great and wonderful and glorious name.” “Hear,” he said, “about the variety of the mountains and of the twelve nations.

“From the first mountain, the black one, those who believed are like this: apostates, and blasphemers against the Lord, and betrayers of the servants of God. For them there is no repentance, but there is death. That is why they are black, for their kind is lawless.

“From the second mountain, the bare one, those who believed are like this: hypocrites, and teachers of wickedness. These too are like the first, for they have no fruit of righteousness. Just as their mountain is without fruit, so people like this have the name, but they are empty of faith, and there is no fruit of truth in them. For these, repentance is open, if they repent quickly. But if they delay, their death will be with the first.”

“Why, sir,” I said, “is there repentance for these, but none for the first? For their deeds are almost the same.” “Repentance is open to these,” he said, “for this reason: they did not blaspheme their Lord, and they did not become betrayers of the servants of God. It was out of desire for gain that they played the hypocrite, and each one taught to suit the desires of people who were sinning. But they will pay some penalty. Yet repentance is open to them, because they did not become blasphemers or betrayers.

“From the third mountain, the one with thorns and thistles, those who believed are like this. Some of them are rich, and others are tangled up in many business affairs. The thistles are the rich, and the thorns are those who are tangled up in business of every kind.

“Those who are tangled up in many kinds of business do not hold fast to the servants of God. They wander away, choked by their own dealings. And the rich find it hard to hold fast to the servants of God, because they are afraid of being asked for something by them. So people like this will find it hard to enter the kingdom of God.
“For just as it is hard to walk among thistles with bare feet, so it is hard for people like this to enter the kingdom of God.

“But for all of these there is repentance, a swift repentance, so that now, in these days, they may make up for what they did not do in earlier times, and do some good. If, then, they repent and do some good, they will live to God. But if they persist in their deeds, they will be handed over to those women, and the women will put them to death.

“From the fourth mountain, the one with many plants, green at the top but dry near the roots, and some withered by the sun, those who believed are like this. Some are double-minded. Others have the Lord on their lips, but do not have him in their heart.

“That is why their foundations are dry and have no power. Only their words are alive, but their works are dead. People like this are neither alive nor dead. So they are like the double-minded. For the double-minded are neither green nor dry, since they are neither alive nor dead.
“For just as these plants withered when they saw the sun, so the double-minded, when they hear of tribulation, worship idols out of cowardice, and are ashamed of the name of their Lord.

“People like this, then, are neither alive nor dead. Yet these too, if they repent quickly, will be able to live. But if they do not repent, they have already been handed over to the women who carry off their life.

“From the fifth mountain, the one that has green plants and is rough, those who believed are like this. They are believers, but slow to learn, and self-willed, and pleased with themselves. They want to know everything, and they know nothing at all.

“Because of this self-will of theirs, understanding departed from them, and senseless folly entered into them. They praise themselves as though they had understanding, and they want to make themselves teachers, though they are fools.

“Because of this haughtiness, then, many have been emptied by exalting themselves. For self-will and empty confidence are a great demon. So many of these were cast out. But some repented and believed, and put themselves under those who have understanding, for they recognized their own folly.

“And for the rest who are like this, repentance is open. For they were not wicked, but rather senseless and without understanding. So if these repent, they will live to God. But if they do not repent, they will dwell with the women who do them evil.
“From the sixth mountain, the one with great and small cracks, and withered plants in the cracks, those who believed are like this.

“Those with the small cracks are the ones who hold something against one another, and their own slanders have withered them in the faith. But many of them have repented. And the rest will repent too, when they hear my commandments. For their slanders are small, and they will repent quickly.

“But those with great cracks persist in their slanders. They hold grudges and nurse their wrath against one another. So these were flung away from the tower and rejected from its building. People like this will find it hard to live.

“Our God and Lord rules over all things and has authority over all his creation. If he holds no grudge against those who confess their sins, but is merciful, does a human being, mortal and full of sins, hold a grudge against another human being, as though he were able to destroy him or to save him?

“And I, the angel of repentance, say to you: all of you who hold to this way, lay it aside and repent, and the Lord will heal your former sins, if you cleanse yourselves of this demon. But if not, you will be handed over to it for death.

“On the seventh mountain the plants were green and cheerful, and the whole mountain was thriving. Every kind of cattle, and the birds of the air, fed on the plants on this mountain, and the plants they fed on grew all the more lush. From this mountain, those who believed are like this.

“They were always simple and innocent and blessed. They held nothing against one another, but always rejoiced in the servants of God. They were clothed with the Holy Spirit of these virgins, and they always had compassion for every person. Out of their own labors they provided for every person, without reproaching anyone and without hesitating.
“So the Lord, seeing their simplicity and all their childlikeness, made them abound in the labors of their hands, and gave them favor in everything they did.

“And I, the angel of repentance, say to you who are like this: remain as you are, and your offspring will never be blotted out. For the Lord has tested you and written you into our number, and all your offspring will dwell with the Son of God. For you have received of his Spirit.
“From the eighth mountain, where the many springs were, and all the Lord’s creation drank from the springs, those who believed are like this.

“They are apostles and teachers who preached to the whole world, and who taught the word of the Lord reverently and purely. They kept nothing at all back for evil desire, but always walked in righteousness and truth, just as they had received the Holy Spirit. So the passage of such people is with the angels.
“From the ninth mountain, the desolate one, which had in it the reptiles and wild beasts that destroy people, those who believed are like this.

“Those with the spots are deacons who served badly. They plundered the livelihood of widows and orphans, and made gain for themselves out of the ministry they had received to carry out. So if they persist in the same desire, they are dead, and there is no hope of life for them. But if they turn back and fulfill their ministry in purity, they will be able to live.

“The scabby ones are those who denied and did not turn back to their Lord. They have become barren and desolate. They do not hold fast to the servants of God, but keep to themselves, and so they destroy their own souls.

“For a vine that is left inside some hedge and gets no care is ruined. The weeds make it desolate, and in time it grows wild, and it is no longer of any use to its master. In the same way, people like this have given up on themselves, and having grown wild, they become useless to their Lord.
“For these, then, there is repentance, if they are not found to have denied from the heart. But if anyone is found to have denied from the heart, I do not know whether he can live.

“And I do not say this for these present days, so that someone may deny and then receive repentance. For it is impossible for anyone to be saved who is going to deny his Lord now. But for those who denied long ago, repentance seems to be open. So if anyone is going to repent, let him be quick, before the tower is finished. Otherwise he will be destroyed by the women and brought to death.

“And the stunted ones are the deceitful and the slanderers. The wild beasts you saw on the mountain are these people too. For just as the wild beasts destroy a person with their venom and kill him, so the words of people like this destroy a person and kill him.

“So these are stunted in their faith, because of the conduct they have within them. But some have repented and been saved. And the rest who are like this can be saved, if they repent. But if they do not repent, they will die at the hands of those women, whose power they have.
“From the tenth mountain, where there were trees sheltering some sheep, those who believed are like this.

“They are bishops and hospitable people, who were always glad to welcome the servants of God into their homes, without hypocrisy. And the bishops always sheltered the needy and the widows by their ministry, without ceasing, and always lived in purity.

“So all these will be sheltered by the Lord at all times. Those who have done these things are glorious before God, and their place is already with the angels, if they continue to the end in serving the Lord.
“From the eleventh mountain, where there were trees full of fruit, adorned with fruit of one kind and another, those who believed are like this.
“They are those who suffered for the name of the Son of God. They suffered willingly, with their whole heart, and gave up their lives.”

“Then why, sir,” I said, “do all the trees have fruit, yet some of their fruits are more beautiful?” “Listen,” he said. “All who have ever suffered for the name are glorious before God, and the sins of all of them have been taken away, because they suffered for the name of the Son of God. But hear why their fruits are varied, and why some surpass the rest.

“Those who were brought before the authorities and questioned,” he said, “and did not deny, but suffered willingly, are all the more glorious before the Lord. Theirs is the fruit that surpasses. But others were cowardly and hesitated. They reasoned in their hearts whether to deny or to confess, and then they suffered. The fruits of these are lesser, because this thought arose in their heart. For it is a wicked thought, that a servant should deny his own lord.

“So take care, you who entertain such thoughts, that this thought does not remain in your hearts, and you die to God. But you who suffer for the sake of the name ought to glorify God, because God has counted you worthy to carry this name, and to have all your sins healed.

“So count yourselves blessed. Rather, consider that you have done a great work, if any of you suffers for God’s sake. The Lord is granting you life, and you do not realize it. For your sins weighed you down, and if you had not suffered for the sake of the Lord’s name, you would have died to God because of your sins.
“I say this to you who hesitate between denying and confessing. Confess that you have a Lord, or else, denying him, you will be handed over to prison.

“If the nations punish their servants when one of them denies his lord, what do you think the Lord will do to you, he who has authority over all things? Take these thoughts out of your hearts, so that you may live to God always.

“From the twelfth mountain, the white one, those who believed are like this. They are like little babies. No evil enters their heart, and they have never known what wickedness is, but have always remained childlike.

“People like this, then, will dwell in the kingdom of God without any question, because in nothing did they defile the commandments of God. They remained childlike all the days of their life, in the same way of thinking.

“So all of you who continue,” he said, “and are like babies, having no evil, will be more glorious than all those I have spoken of. For all babies are glorious before God, and they come first with him. Blessed are you, then, all who put wickedness away from yourselves and put on innocence. You will live to God before all others.”

When he had finished the parables of the mountains, I said to him, “Sir, now tell me about the stones that were taken from the plain and set in the building in place of the stones that were taken out of the tower. Tell me also about the round stones that were set in the building, and about those that are still round.”
“Hear about all these as well,” he said. “The stones that were taken from the plain and set in the building of the tower, in place of those that were cast out, are the roots of the white mountain.

“Since those who believed from the white mountain were all found innocent, the lord of the tower ordered these stones from the roots of this mountain to be put into the building of the tower. For he knew that if these stones went into the building of the tower, they would stay bright, and not one of them would turn black.

“But if he had added stones from the other mountains, he would have had to visit that tower again and cleanse it. Yet all these have been found white, those who have believed and those who are going to believe, for they are of the same kind. Blessed is this kind, because it is innocent.

“Now hear also about the round, bright stones. They too are all from the white mountain. But hear why they were found round. Their riches have clouded them a little from the truth, and darkened them. Yet they never departed from God, and no evil word came out of their mouth, but all uprightness and the virtue of truth.

“The Lord saw their mind, that they could favor the truth and also remain good. So he ordered their wealth to be cut down, yet not taken from them altogether, so that they might be able to do some good with what was left to them. And they will live to God, because they are of a good kind. That is why they were cut down a little and set in the building of this tower.

“But the rest, who have still remained round and have not been fitted into that building, because they have not yet received the seal, were put back in their place. For they were found to be very round.

“This world must be cut away from them, and the vanities of their riches, and then they will fit into the kingdom of God. For they must enter the kingdom of God, because the Lord has blessed this innocent kind. So not one of this kind will be lost. For even if one of them is tempted by the most wicked devil and does some wrong, he will quickly run back to his Lord.
“I, the angel of repentance, count you all happy, all of you who are innocent as infants, because your portion is good and honored before God.

“And I say to all of you who have received this seal: hold to simplicity, and do not keep offenses in mind. Do not remain in your malice, or in the bitter memory of offenses. Become of one spirit, every one of you, and mend these evil cracks and take them away from among you, so that the lord of the sheep may rejoice over them.
“And he will rejoice if all are found sound, and none of them have fallen away. But if some of them are found to have fallen away, woe to the shepherds.

“And if the shepherds themselves are found to have fallen away, what will they say to the master of the flock? That they fell away because of the sheep? They will not be believed. For it is past belief that a shepherd should suffer anything from his sheep. Rather, they will be punished for their lie. And I am a shepherd too, and I must most strictly give an account for you.

“So mend yourselves, while the tower is still being built. The Lord dwells in those who love peace, for peace is truly dear to him. But he is far from the quarrelsome and from those who are lost in malice. So give the spirit back to him whole, as you received it.

“For if you give a fuller a new garment, whole, and you want to get it back whole, but the fuller returns it to you torn, will you accept it? Will you not flare up at once and go after him with reproaches? You will say, ‘I gave you a whole garment. Why have you torn it and made it useless? Because of the tear you made in it, it cannot be used.’ Will you not say all these things to the fuller, then, about the tear he has made in your garment?

“If, then, you are so grieved over your garment, and complain that you did not get it back whole, what do you think the Lord will do to you? He gave you the spirit whole, and you have made it wholly useless, so that it can be of no use at all to its Lord. For its use became useless when it was spoiled by you. Will not the Lord of that spirit, then, punish you with death for this deed of yours?”
“Certainly,” I said. “He will so punish all those he finds holding on to the memory of offenses.”
“Do not trample on his mercy,” he said. “Honor him instead, because he is so patient with your offenses, and is not like you. So repent, with a repentance that is of use to you.

“All these things that are written above, I, the Shepherd, the angel of repentance, have shown and spoken to the servants of God. So if you believe, and hear my words, and walk in them, and set your ways right, you will be able to live. But if you remain in malice and in the memory of offenses, no one of that kind will live to God. All these things that I was to say have now been said to you.”

The Shepherd himself said to me, “Have you asked me everything?” And I said, “Yes, sir.” “Then why,” he said, “have you not asked me about the hollows left by the stones that were set in the building, the hollows we filled up?” And I said, “I forgot, sir.”

“Hear about them now,” he said. “These are the ones who have now heard my commandments and have repented with all their heart. And when the Lord saw that their repentance was good and pure, and that they could continue in it, he ordered their former sins to be blotted out. For these hollows were their sins, and they were made level, so that they would not show.”
orientation: The Shepherd, the angel of repentance, now lives in Hermas’s house. He takes Hermas to a mountain in Arcadia to show him, in greater detail, the building of the tower that the Church showed him before.

title: The angel's final charge and the virgins' guardianship
english: After I had written out this book, the angel who had handed me over to the Shepherd came to the house where I was. He sat down on the bed, and the Shepherd stood at his right hand.

Then the angel called me and said, “I handed you and your household over to this Shepherd, so that you could be protected by him.” “Yes, sir,” I said. “If, then, you want to be protected from every harm and every cruelty,” he said, “and to have success in every good work and word, and every virtue of righteousness, walk in his commandments, which I have given you. And you will be able to master all wickedness.

“For if you keep his commandments, every desire and sweetness of this world will be subject to you, and success will follow you in every good undertaking. Take his maturity and modesty into yourself. Tell everyone that he stands in great honor and dignity with the Lord, that he is a ruler of great power, and mighty in his office. To him alone, through the whole world, the power of repentance has been given. Does he seem powerful to you? Yet all of you despise his maturity and the respect he shows you.”
I said to him, “Sir, ask him yourself whether, since he has been in my house, I have done anything out of order to offend him.”

“I too know,” he said, “that you have done nothing out of order, and that you will not. That is why I say these things to you, so that you may persevere. For here, before me, he has thought well of you. But you are to tell these words to the others, so that those who have repented, or are going to repent, may think as you do. Then he may speak well of them here before me, and I before the Lord.”
“And I, sir,” I said, “declare the mighty works of the Lord to every person. And I hope that all who have sinned before, if they hear these things, will gladly repent and recover life.”

“Continue in this ministry, then,” he said, “and bring it to completion. All who carry out his commandments will have life, and great honor here with the Lord. But all who do not keep his commandments are fleeing from their own life, and they set themselves against him. They do not follow his commandments, but hand themselves over to death, and each one of them becomes guilty of his own blood. But I tell you to serve these commandments, and you will have a remedy for your sins.

“I have sent you these virgins to live with you, for I saw that they were kindly toward you. So you have them as helpers, to make you better able to keep his commandments. For these commandments cannot be kept without these virgins. I see that they are glad to be with you. Even so, I will instruct them not to leave your house at all.

“Only cleanse your house, for in a clean house they will gladly live. They are clean and chaste and hardworking, and all of them have favor with the Lord. So if they find your house pure, they will stay with you. But if the least defilement comes in, they will leave your house at once. For these virgins have no love at all for any defilement.”

I said to him, “Sir, I hope that I will please them, so that they will always be glad to live in my house. And just as he to whom you handed me over finds no fault with me, neither will they find fault with me.”
The angel said to the Shepherd, “I know that the servant of God wants to live. He will keep these commandments, and he will settle the virgins in purity.”

When he had said this, he handed me over to the Shepherd again. Then he called the virgins and said to them, “I see that you are glad to live in this man’s house. So I entrust him and his household to you, so that you will not leave his house at all.” The virgins heard these words gladly.

Then he said to me, “Bear yourself bravely in this ministry. Declare the mighty works of the Lord to every person, and you will have favor in this ministry. Whoever walks in these commandments will live and will be happy in his life. But whoever neglects them will not live and will be unhappy in his life.

“Tell all who are able to do right not to stop. It is useful for them to practice good works. And I say that every person ought to be rescued from hardship. For the one who is in want, and suffers hardship in his daily life, is in great torment and need.

“So whoever rescues such a soul from need wins great joy for himself. For the one who is harassed by hardship of this kind is tormented, and racks himself, with the same torment as a man in chains. Many, because of calamities like these, when they cannot bear them, bring death on themselves. So whoever knows of such a person’s calamity and does not rescue him commits a great sin and becomes guilty of his blood.

“Do good works, then, all of you who have received from the Lord, so that the structure of the tower is not finished while you delay to do them. For it is because of you that the work of its construction has been interrupted. So unless you make haste to do right, the tower will be finished, and you will be shut out.”
When he had finished speaking with me, he rose from the bed, took the Shepherd and the virgins, and went away. But he told me that he would send that Shepherd and the virgins back to my house.
orientation: The book ends in Hermas’s own house. The angel who first handed him over to the Shepherd comes, sits on the bed, and gives him a last charge about the commandments, the virgins who are to live with him, and doing good before the tower is finished.
